key_insight: In RL with verifiable rewards, momentum can help if the EMA coefficient is set large enough to stay in a safe, non-overshooting regime; otherwise sampling noise can hide its benefit.
engineering_relevance: For LLM post-training, tuning momentum upward can yield measurable accuracy gains and should be treated as a practical hyperparameter rather than a default setting.
method: Analyze RLVR as a bandit problem with bias-corrected EMA momentum.
Prove that larger \u03b2 accelerates optimization when exact gradients are used and overshoot is avoided.
Show that under sampled gradients, shrinking learning rate alone can wash out the momentum gain, while jointly increasing \u03b2 preserves it.
evidence_signal: Bandit simulations and RLVR experiments on Qwen3-4B-Base and Qwen2.5-32B validate the theory, with larger \u03b2_1 improving mean validation accuracy by nearly 2 percentage points on the larger model.
watch_item: The benefit depends on keeping \u03b7/(1-\u03b2) in a safe regime; too-small or poorly matched settings can obscure gains or cause overshoot.
paper_title: When Does Momentum Help in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards?
